what_this_is: Iso-contours of a SOLVED interstitial fluid pressure field over the same real Xenium GBM section as tumor.glb. Not illustrative: the field is the output of tmesim.physics.pressure.solve_ifp on the reconstruction, and the only transformation applied before contouring is a stated local mean (see display_coarse_grain_um).
model: steady-state screened Poisson  -div(K grad p) + (a+d) p = a p_v  with leaky-vessel Starling sources from the measured ENDOTHELIAL cell positions, lymphatic drainage suppressed inside the tumour, Dirichlet p=0 at the border and outside the tissue mask; 5-point finite volume, harmonic-mean face conductances, sparse direct solve
parameter_note: Transport parameters are order-of-magnitude biological values, not patient-calibrated (see tmesim/physics/pressure.py). The GEOMETRY driving the solve is measured; the coefficients are not fitted to this section.
citation: 10x Genomics Xenium In Situ, FFPE Human Brain Glioblastoma with Add-on (Xenium Analyzer v1.3.0), sample Xenium_V1_FFPE_Human_Brain_Glioblastoma_With_Addon, CC BY 4.0.
display_coarse_grain_note: Contours are of the solved field's local mean over a 250 um Gaussian window taken across tissue nodes only. The raw field's structure is per-vessel (screening length ~7.1 um) and lies far below one screen pixel at the zoom the page draws the whole 8.1 mm section at, so it is averaged for display. No solver term was changed. Because this is a MEAN, the level values below are much lower than raw_field_max_mmhg.

screening_length_um.definition: L = sqrt(K/(a+d)), the screened-Poisson operator's decay length, evaluated node-by-node on this section from the shipped coefficients
screening_length_um.correction_note: Supersedes a figure of '~60 um' published in earlier versions of this file, which was ~8.5x too large. The measured value is 7.1 um.

resolution_caveat: WHAT THE MESH ACTUALLY RESOLVES, stated because the solver name alone would overstate it. The screening length above (~7.1 um) is BELOW this export's grid spacing of 12 um, at 99.8 % of tissue nodes, and the reaction term dominates the diagonal (median (a+d)*dx^2/K = 2.87). Each node therefore relaxes toward its own local algebraic equilibrium a*p_v/(a+d) with the Laplacian barely coupling neighbours: the solved field correlates with that pointwise limit at r = 0.9 on this section. So this IS a real solve of the stated equation — nothing authored, nothing fitted to this patient — but at this resolution it is closer to a pointwise nonlinear map of the vascular-density field than to a resolved transport solve, and the margin pressure gradient that carries the Jain effect into the convection term is not resolved. Measured in results/ifp_validation.md §5.1-5.2 (GBM, dx = 12 um). Refining the mesh does not currently fix this and is not free: the field is not grid-converged either.
transform: Identical to tumor.glb's, then expressed in the page's standing-up frame: scene x=(x_um-x_mid)*s, scene y=(y_um-y_mid)*s with s=0.00032147042 units/um. Uniform, isotropic, centred — no rotation or stretch.
